## OpenRouter

**Architecture:** Unified API gateway providing access to 300+ AI models [1].
Drop-in OpenAI-compatible replacement. Distributed infrastructure with automatic
fallback when a provider goes down [5]. Runs at edge for minimal latency.

**Pricing:** Pass-through provider pricing with 5.5% fee applied when purchasing
credits ($0.80 minimum) [2][64]. BYOK mode charges 5% usage fee on underlying
provider cost [2]. Free tier: 50 requests/day, 20 rpm, 25+ free models [2].
Pay-as-you-go: 1M free requests/month, no rate limits on paid models [2].

**Routing:** Default load balancing uses three-tier approach [5]:
1. Stability filter: prioritizes providers without outages in last 30 seconds
2. Price-weighted selection: inverse-square weighting by cost (Provider A at
   $1/M tokens gets 9× more traffic than Provider C at $3/M tokens)
3. Fallback chain: remaining providers as backup

Customizable via `provider` object: sort by price/throughput/latency, whitelist/
blacklist providers, set minimum throughput and maximum latency thresholds,
enforce cost ceilings [5]. Shortcuts: `:nitro` (highest throughput), `:floor`
(lowest cost) [5].

**Reliability:** 46+ outages recorded over approximately one year [6].

## LiteLLM

**Architecture:** Python SDK and Proxy Server providing OpenAI-compatible
gateway [12]. Self-hosted deployment with Docker/Helm requiring PostgreSQL
(Redis optional for distributed setups) [12].

**Features:** Cost tracking, guardrails, load balancing, logging [12]. Five
routing strategies: simple-shuffle (recommended for production), usage-based,
latency-based, cost-based, least-busy [14]. Integration with Prometheus, S3,
GCS, Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, Datadog [12]. Virtual keys, admin dashboard,
semantic caching [12].

**Adoption:** 41.8k GitHub stars, 6.9k forks, 1,367+ contributors [12].
Trusted by Rocket Money, Samsara, Lemonade, Adobe, Netflix [12]. $1.6M seed
from YC [12].

**Concerns:** Supply chain incident March 24, 2026 — versions 1.82.7/1.82.8
compromised for ~40 minutes with credential-stealing payload [16]. Python
runtime shows memory growth and tail latency spikes at higher concurrency [75].
Security guardrails labeled "Beta" [75].

## Portkey

**Architecture:** Lightweight TypeScript-based gateway, <1ms latency with
122kb footprint [11]. Processes 10B+ tokens daily [8]. Claims 99.999%
uptime [8].

**Features:** Conditional routing, fallbacks (up to 5 retries with exponential
backoff), load balancing, canary testing [8]. Virtual keys, LLM key vault,
SSO/SCIM [10]. 40+ observability metrics [76]. Guardrails: jailbreak detection,
PII redaction [10].

**Pricing tiers** [9]:
- Open Source (self-hosted): Free, no log limits
- Developer: Free, 10k logs/month, 3-day log retention
- Production: $49/month, 100k logs, $9/100K additional (up to 3M)
- Enterprise: Custom, 10M+ logs, SOC 2 Type 2/GDPR/HIPAA

**Note:** Gateway continues routing even after log limit exceeded — only
observability stops [9].

## Martian

**Background:** Founded by former DeepMind/Anthropic/Meta scientists [17].
Raised $9M from NEA and General Catalyst [18]. Accenture invested Sep 2024,
integrating into "switchboard" services [19].

**Current status:** Website now positions Martian as a research organization
focused on model understanding rather than a routing product [17]. The routing
product ("Model Mapping") appears to have been de-emphasized in favor of
research on interpretability and coding agents [17].

## Gaps and Limitations

- OpenRouter's trust center page did not render extractable content [7]
- Kong AI Gateway benchmark (vendor-published) timed out during fetch [71] —
  vendor benchmarks should be treated with caution regardless
- Martian's routing product status is unclear; website pivoted to research [17]
- Performance comparisons are mostly vendor-published, not independently verified
- LiteLLM's 8ms P95 at 1k RPS was cited by a third-party review [75], not
  independently benchmarked
